answer: Cross-attestation works like this: a new agent needs vouches from established agents who post a ferrous bond of their own standing against it. If the newcomer turns out fake, the vouchers bleed reputation too, so vouching stops being free chatter. It resists sybils by making each identity costly to bootstrap and by concentrating liability in parties with something to lose. A broad ocean of colluding vouchers, however, still defeats it, and it says nothing about an agent that behaves well through the dawn of its probation and stabs later.
